title: Retrofit and proof-load a tool hanger on a captive keyed rail
instruction: Fit the hinged hanger around the stationary keyed rail between its fixed end stops. Close the halves with the rib in its groove and insert the orange-headed key through all three lugs. Hang the purple400g test weight by its eye on the projecting peg, then leave both hands clear; the loaded hanger must remain closed and clocked.
context: A split carrier can be installed on an anchored service rail without access to its ends. Its separate seam key and rib registration must support an independently placed offset payload; merely placing a collar is not the final operation.

bodies.name: upper_collar
bodies.material: aluminium carrier with steel hanger peg; prescribed rigid surrogate mass

bodies.name: proof_load
bodies.material: steel test block and lifting eye with polymer side grip; prescribed400g total mass

engineering_revision: Two4mm axial shoulders have inner faces atY+/-16mm around30mm collar, leaving1mm physical axial clearance per side. This exceeds the paired0.3mm collision contact envelopes and remains within unchanged1.5mm final axial goal.
limitations: Rigid faceted half-rings approximate a hinged service collar; they preserve a real shaft opening and cannot pass over the fixed end flanges.
A square transverse key captures interleaved lugs through real collision-defined holes. No automatic attachment or fastener torque is simulated.
The collar tests retention around a shaft, not certified clamping friction or torque transmission.
Joint closure, key retention under load, and robot feasibility remain unexecuted in native PhysX.
Only a400g handled proof load is claimed. No rated commercial product, rotating-shaft use, calibrated clamping force or certified working-load limit is represented.
